newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX COB electricity lower, PV higher with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX COB electricity lower, PV higher with cash.

text.p: NYMEX California-Oregon Border(COB) electricity futures settled lower Tuesday, while Palo Verde (PV) power contracts finished higher in line with spot western physical prices.
June COB futures settled down 16 cents at $13.99 after posting a high of $14.35. July COB ended down 16 cents at $16.14. Deferred COB months finished three to 25 cents lower.
June PV futures settled up 30 cents at $19.15, trimming a 65 cent gain. July PV ended up 15 cents at $23.35. Other PV contracts finished down five to up 20 cents.

Day-ahead firm, peak cash values at COB eased following yesterday's rally, ending at $16.50-17.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) down 50 cents from Tuesday, while those at PV rose sharply to $19.00-21.00 from Tuesday's $18.50-19.50.
Traders said spot power supply in the West remained tight as Bonneville Power Administration continued to withhold sales of electricity during morning and evening peak hours.
Moreover, Canada's B.C. Hydro pulled out of the U.S. spot market this week due to the need to reduce in-flows at its Arrow project on the Columbia River in British Columbia.
Power plant outages, higher natural gas prices, and firm air-conditioning demand in parts of the Southwest continued to lift spot PV prices, market sources said.
About 4,000 MW of generating capacity in the Southwest are currently offline for repairs or maintenance.
June Henry Hub natural gas futures settled up 4.2 cents at $2.184 per million British thermal units.
Brokers and traders said June power contracts would continue to take cue from cash prices and natural gas futures.
"If June gas fails to break $2.210, PV could top out," said a Houston futures trader.
Separately, a 550 megawatt (MW) unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming was set to restart tomorrow Thursday after being shut last week for repairs.
The Northwest was forecast to see some clearing Thursday and Friday, but some areas were expected to cool considerably over the next several days.

By Friday, temperatures would average four to six degrees Fahrenheit below normal in the western region and 10 to 16 degrees below normal in the eastern region. Temperatures were expected to moderate toward near normal levels by Sunday.

In the Southwest, some air conditioning demand for power was expected to continue, with forecasts calling for readings in the southern area to average two to four degrees above normal through Friday, although temperatures in the northern and eastern sections were expected to run eight to 12 degrees below normal during the same period.
NYMEX estimated 529 COB and 169 PV contracts were sold.
